I can’t quote the “current” California statute or certify compliance right now because your request requires checking up‑to‑date law and I don’t have browsing or legal‑database access in this session. I also can’t assess whether your checkout flow is compliant without seeing the actual flow details. I can, however:

- Explain what I’m unable to do here (and why).
- Give a practical, non‑legal checklist of the typical requirements you should verify for California automatic‑renewal / negative‑option billing rules.
- Offer how I can help next (review pasted statute text or your checkout flow, or re‑run the check if you enable web access).

What I cannot do here
- I cannot quote the California statute “currently governing” automatic‑renewal cancellation as of 2032‑01‑06 because that is a current legal fact that must be looked up and I have no browsing/legal‑database tools available.
- I cannot give a definitive compliance determination without (a) the applicable statute or recent authoritative guidance and (b) the concrete checkout flow / wording / UX to evaluate.

Useful checklist — items you should verify (for California AR/negative‑option billing)
Note: this is general compliance guidance, not legal advice. You should confirm the exact statutory text and any recent amendments or agency guidance, or consult counsel.

- Clear, conspicuous disclosure of material terms before purchase
  - The fact the purchase enrolls the consumer in an automatic renewal or continuous service.
  - The recurring price, billing cadence, and any additional fees.
  - The initial term and renewal term(s).
  - How to cancel (specific method).

- Affirmative consent (consumer must take an affirmative action)
  - The user must affirmatively consent to the automatic renewal terms (checkbox that is unchecked by default, or another unambiguous opt‑in), with the disclosure proximate to the buy/confirm action.

- Acknowledgement/confirmation after purchase
  - Provide a written acknowledgement (email or other durable medium) that restates the material terms and provides cancellation instructions and contact information.

- Easy, simple cancellation mechanism
  - Cancellation method(s) should be at least as easy as enrollment (e.g., online cancellation if the consumer subscribed online).
  - If you require phone cancellation, provide a toll‑free number and reasonable hours; do not impose unnecessarily burdensome steps.
  - Provide immediate confirmation of cancellation.

- Reminder notice before renewal (if required)
  - Some laws/regulations require a reminder or notice before an upcoming renewal (check statute for timing/thresholds).

- Free trials, introductory offers, and negative options
  - Disclose how the trial converts, when billing will begin, amount to be charged, and how to cancel before conversion.

- Changes to terms / price increases
  - Disclose whether renewal price may change and how the consumer will be notified/consent obtained for increases.

- Recordkeeping and evidence
  - Keep records showing the disclosures presented, the affirmative consent, the acknowledgement, and cancellation requests and confirmations.

- Billing and merchant obligations
  - Provide clear merchant contact information; handle refunds and disputes per statute and payment‑network rules.

How I can help now
- If you paste the text of the California statute (or a link and you paste the text) I can quote it and analyze it against your checkout flow.
- If you paste screenshots or the exact wording and flow of your checkout (what disclosures appear, checkboxes, confirmation email text, cancellation method), I can analyze it against the checklist above and point out likely gaps and suggested fixes.
- If you later enable browsing or provide an authoritative copy of the statute/guidance, I can compare that exact statute to your flow and give a more definite evaluation.

Recommendation
- Because state automatic‑renewal law can change and often depends on precise statutory language and agency or court interpretation, please either: (A) paste the statute text or the checkout flow here, or (B) enable a current lookup so I can fetch the controlling statute and cite it before assessing compliance. Also consider getting a qualified attorney to confirm compliance before relying on the result.
